text:
Marta: Quick RFC follow-up — I prototyped a tiny proxy that does selective payload rewrites to support incremental schema evolution (rename/add fields) so v2 clients can talk to v1 services without a heavy adapter. Thoughts?

Kevin: curious how invasive the rules are. Is this just a mapping table + simple transforms? or full JS-like transform logic?

Marta: mapping table + small transform funcs. Keep it intentionally limited: no arbitrary scripting, only safe operations (rename, default, drop, jsonpath move). config looks like: ```
rules:
  - match: requests[].user_id
    rename: requests[].uid
  - match: metadata.timestamp_ms
    default: 0
```

Priyaa: 👍 love the minimal surface. Two concerns: telemetry/safety (how do we know rewrites don't degrade ML model inputs?) and perf — extra network hop + CPU.

Marta: perf measured on prototype: ~0.4ms median processing on p95 small payloads, < 1ms for larger ones. We'll co-locate the proxy as a sidecar to avoid extra hop in most deployments. Telemetry plan below.

Kevin: sidecar + config iteration sounds fine. For larger responses (embeddings, long tokens) need streaming compatibility — does the proxy support chunked passes or only whole-body?

Marta: initially whole-body only. Streaming is a future step but we can short-circuit streaming endpoints (bypass proxy) during canary.

Jules: We need a clear opt-in header so clients can opt into compatibility translations and we can sample. Suggest `X-Compat-Sample: 0.05` or `X-Compat-Mode: staged` header.

Priyaa: +1 on header. Also add a per-tenant feature flag to disable for specific customers if we detect regressions.

Sam-bot: deploy-bot triggered: prototype image pushed to gcr/redwood/proxy-lite:pr-128 (sha: abc123).

Kevin: rollback plan? If we see bad signals we need immediate kill switch. Maybe support two modes: `transform` and `passthrough`, and a global feature toggle in FF service.

Marta: agreed. Kill switch + per-tenant opt-out. Telemetry: we emit a small event with: `rewrite.applied`, `rewrite.rule_id`, `request.hash`, `sampling.rate`, `tenant.id` (PII-safe hashed). We'll tie to existing eval infra so QA can run prompt sets against transformed traffic.

Priyaa: make sure we also attach a checksum of original payload so we can replay exact original inputs to offline tests. Also include a confidence flag when transforms may be lossy.

Marta: will add `rewrite.lossy=true|false` and `original.checksum`. Implementation detail: use SHA256 hex truncated to 16 chars for checksum.

Kevin: security note: avoid adding new surface for injection. Limit transforms to declarative operations, validate JSONPath targets, max-depth limits, and a strict allowlist of fields.

Marta: yes, validated. We'll run fuzzing tests for transform rules and run existing unit tests with the proxy in front.

Jules: rollout plan suggestion:
- Stage 0: internal dev only (feature flag on)
- Stage 1: 1% tenant sampling via `X-Compat-Sample` header + telemetry collection for 48h
- Stage 2: 10% tenants, automated regression checks on key metrics (latency, model-quality evals)
- Stage 3: gradual ramp + per-tenant opt-in window

Priyaa: add a canary alert: if `model-quality.delta` > threshold OR `error.rate` increases by x, auto-toggle to passthrough for sampled tenants.

Marta: implemented in prototype: `quality_delta_alert` and `auto_passthrough_on_alert=true` flags.

Kevin: one more: how do SDKs discover whether the proxy translation exists? We should expose a capability header from the server side so new SDKs can retry with compat header only when server advertises support. e.g., server sends `Server-Supports-Compat: true` on handshake.

Marta: good idea. We'll add `Server-Supports-Compat` and `Compat-Config-Version` to health endpoint. SDKs can then use a try-and-sample approach.

Priyaa: docs/ops checklist please. Include: rule audit, telemetry dashboards, runbook for toggling feature flag, list of safe transforms, and a compatibility test matrix.

Marta: will open a follow-up PR with checklist + small playbook. For now, I'll run the 1% sample internally tomorrow and post metrics.

Kevin: cool. If results look good we can expand to external beta. Thanks Marta. :thumbsup:

Marta: thanks all — will update when metrics land.
